cards.text: Jephthah, the leader from Gilead, just beat the Ammonites. Then the men of Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes, gather up and cross the Jordan to Zaphon. And friend, they did NOT come to say congratulations.

cards.question: The men of Ephraim confront Jephthah. What's their complaint?

answers.text: He fought the Ammonites without calling them
He kept the Ammonite land for Gilead
He made a vow without asking them

cards.text: Then they tell him, "We will burn your house down with you inside!" That's showing up after the move is done, mad nobody asked you to carry a box, and bringing a MATCH.

cards.question: Jephthah answers Ephraim: he says he called them for help against the Ammonites, and they did not save him.

cards.text: Jephthah says when he saw nobody was coming to save him, he risked his life and crossed over to the Ammonites himself.

cards.question: Jephthah tells Ephraim the ___ delivered the Ammonites into his hand.
Jephthah finishes with one question for the men of Ephraim. What does he ask them?

answers.text: Why have you come today to fight against me
Why did you wait so long to answer my call
Why should Gilead share its spoils with you

cards.text: Talking's done. Jephthah gathers all the men of Gilead and fights Ephraim.

cards.question: In the fight between Gilead and Ephraim, Ephraim's army beats the men of Gilead.
The text gives a reason the men of Gilead struck Ephraim down: something the Ephraimites had said. What was it?

answers.text: You Gileadites are fugitives in Ephraim
You Gileadites are cowards in battle
You Gileadites have no real leader

cards.text: Then the Gileadites capture the fords of the Jordan leading to Ephraim. Any Ephraimite running from the fight has to come through them.

cards.question: Whenever a man at the fords asks to cross over, the Gileadites ask him, "Are you an ___?"

cards.text: If the man says no, they tell him, "Please say Shibboleth." And if it comes out "Sibboleth," they know.

cards.question: At the fords, why does saying "Sibboleth" give a man away as an Ephraimite?

answers.text: He could not pronounce it correctly
He did not know what it meant
He answered too slowly at the ford

cards.question: The Gileadites let a man go home if he says "Sibboleth" at the fords.

cards.text: They seize him and kill him right there at the fords of the Jordan. At that time, 42,000 Ephraimites are killed, and friend, that one sits heavy.
Jephthah judges Israel six years. Then he dies.

cards.question: When Jephthah dies, he is buried in the hill country of Ephraim.

cards.text: Then three more judges come, one after another: Ibzan of Bethlehem for seven years, Elon the Zebulunite for ten, and Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, for eight. Abdon had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys. SEVENTY. That's a family that never once had to ask, "Can somebody give me a ride?"

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "Are you an ___?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Judges 12:3 has Jephthah say "When I saw that you would not save me." The card widens this to "nobody was coming to save him." That makes it about everyone, not just Ephraim. It also hides that his own people fought with him ("My people and I," 12:2).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Cards 4 and 5 have just said Ephraim didn't come to save Jephthah. That rules out the wrong answer "Ephraimites," so the card is really a pick between two answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain retelling with no voice, especially cards 5, 8 and 11. The only real jokes are on cards 3 and 19. The stretch about Jephthah's reply and the fords (cards 4 to 13) has room for his reactions and disbelief without muddying a fact.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card adds that any fleeing Ephraimite "has to come through them." Judges 12:5 says only that the Gileadites captured the fords leading to Ephraim and questioned the fugitives who asked to cross. It never says this was the only way across.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
